verified_assertions: Replaying an artifact with missing stored bytes after server restart returns 200 duplicate, restores exact bytes, and retains one metadata row plus one artifact.attached event.
Same artifact ID and bytes with changed type, content-type or encoding returns 409.
Corrupted stored bytes return 500; identical replay restores checksum-correct bytes.
Wrong SHA-256, oversize bytes, traversal ID, missing run/attempt and missing sanitization fail without leftover bytes or artifact metadata.
Gzip download preserves exact compressed bytes and Content-Encoding; read-only token cannot download evidence.
A real HTTP upload aborted after the server receives partial request bytes creates no artifact bytes, metadata or attachment event.
Injected child process exit 73 at registerArtifact entry occurs after file rename and before metadata transaction; on restart identical upload recovers with 201 and exact bytes.
Usage duplicate sample returns 200; conflicting sample returns 409; restart does not double-count.
Provider-reported cost 40, estimate 900 and manual unknown remain distinguishable in by_source; legacy all-source cost is 940.
Coverage preserves NULL metrics and counts unknowns, including zero samples for an attempt with no usage.
limitations: Artifact uploads remain opt-in and bounded-buffered rather than streamed to disk.
The crash test injects process.exit(73) at one specific rename/metadata boundary; it is not a random crash or power-loss campaign.
A process exit during a temp write may leave an unacknowledged .upload-* file; no startup sweeper or retention worker was added.
Temporary file data is fsynced before rename; parent directory fsync and physical power-loss durability were not verified.
Legacy top-level usage totals combine all sources and can double-count an estimate of already reported consumption; use by_source.provider_reported for provider-reported charges.
No dispatcher, provider, GitHub or Trello integration or real-session upload was exercised.
